reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a perfectly flat, zero-valued signal across all scales, with no discernible period, trend, curvature, or amplitude variation. All four reference candidates exhibit identical morphology: a constant line at robust-standardized value 0.0, extending over 1, 3, 3, and 5 nominal cycles respectively. Stability is maximal—no fluctuations, noise, or outliers are visible; the MAD and all shape descriptors (roughness, slope, curvature) are exactly zero in the catalog, confirming absolute stationarity. Peaks and troughs are absent; the signal lacks any local extrema. The only acceptable variation is none—any deviation from exact zero, however small, would constitute an anomaly under this definition. This reflects a difference-stationary series where the original raw data has been differenced to remove trend and seasonality, leaving pure white noise centered at zero; here, even that residual noise is absent, indicating an unusually clean, deterministic baseline segment. The consistent zero level across disjoint intervals confirms that the normalization (median/MAD robust standardization) succeeded and that the underlying process is truly stationary in mean and scale over these windows.
